record.title: Rodolfo Robles selective physical gate blockade during migrant caravan, October2018
record.scope: Rodolfo Robles bridge entry into Mexico for caravan participants; no bilateral frontier-wide prohibition.
record.crossings: Rodolfo Robles bridge; Tecún Umán–Ciudad Hidalgo
record.movement: Caravan participants seeking entry without migration documents; selected applicants admitted. Later vehicle restriction separately described but its onset/end unknown.
record.exceptions: Morning asylum applicants admitted; children and adults admitted in groups after afternoon closure. River crossings occurred. No all-person prohibition asserted.
record.imposing_authority: Mexican Federal Police and immigration authorities
record.enforcement: Police physically shut metal gate and prevented mass passage; beyond routine document checks alone.
record.consequences: People remained on bridge or crossed river; no quantified harm or displacement estimate assigned.
record.relationship: Part-promotion of R3-AM-L007 October2018 component; January20 2020 component remains unresolved and distinct from R3-AM-007. October28 candidate held for overlap.
record.official_rationale: Authorities sought ordered admission under migration/refugee procedures rather than mass undocumented passage.
record.context: Caravan confrontation and physical gate barricade; Guatemalan preceding barrier reported but not separately counted.
record.uncertainty: Official morning denial is preserved alongside later physical blockade; these concern different times and blanket versus selective scope. Same-day admissions prevent continuous total-closure inference. November7 pedestrian reopening report is only normal-by evidence; vehicles remained barred then. October28 possible renewed phase is held separately.

historical.duration_note: Unknown scoped endpoint and continuity; publication dates not treated as reopening dates.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: La Jornada correspondent reports physical gate closure after the caravan confrontation; actual selective obstruction supported.
Friday October 19 about 13:30 is described in the October 20 article.
Same-day selected admissions and pedestrian normal-by November 7 do not establish a single endpoint.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Migration control and ordered admission stated by authorities support Migration.
Morning admission of 100 asylum applicants and blanket-closure denial precede the afternoon gate closure; later vehicle ban is not backdated.
Selected admissions contradict a continuous all-person 20-day closure. Retain unknown end and no interval.
